title: Reuse architecture knowledge, device snapshots and measurements at different scopes
applies_when: Onboarding a new GPU, reusing hardware knowledge across devices/hosts/drivers/workloads, or reproducing a model issue on a different accelerator architecture.
lesson: Reuse official architecture semantics by architecture and document revision; query actual SKU/partition capacities and host topology separately. Keep empirical rates bound to probe, precision, shape, layout, cache regime, runtime and power/clock/load conditions. Reuse the method on another device, then run a cheap canary before transferring numerical rates. For model reproductions, record the realized backend and cache format, not only matching API flags: DeepSeek-V4.1 may default to SM100 Mega Attention while a Hopper report uses FlashMLA sparse. If explicitly selecting another supported backend, establish its own matched baseline before comparing. Preserve unavailable fields and known query limitations so the next agent does not repeat unsupported probes without a relevant environment change.
avoid_when: Matching architecture or marketing names does not prove equal SM counts, bandwidth, partition size or connectivity. A live inventory or empty process list is not an allocation/idleness guarantee; check load and memory too, especially with container visibility restrictions. Negotiated link metadata is not payload bandwidth, and an empirical reference is not a physical ceiling. A pass on another default backend does not refute the reported path. Even the same named backend can retain architecture-dependent cache/layout code; forcing its name does not establish cross-architecture equivalence or performance.

evidence.note: Documents device identity, query availability, link and runtime-dependent management observations. Supports cheap per-device revalidation, not transfer of private benchmark rates.
Documents timing and effective-bandwidth interpretation, memory hierarchy and performance dependencies. Supports scoped measurement reuse; no per-device performance number is asserted here.

The pinned selector distinguishes explicit FlashMLA sparse, FlashInfer and Mega Attention; eligible SM100 defaults to Mega, with topology/build fallbacks. This explains why the same API settings need not reach the same backend. Source mechanism, not a GPU verdict or measured discovery gain.

FlashMLA sparse accepts capability major9/10; Mega only major10 and has a different attention interface plus its NVFP4 compressed record. Supported backend names are not proof of identical executed kernels or layout. No claim that the reported Hopper issue is fixed or disproved.
